$comment: Domestic corporation income tax parameters (CREATE / CREATE MORE era).

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 27(A), as amended by RA 11534 (CREATE) and RA 12066 (CREATE MORE)
rcit.notes: 20% applies when net taxable income ≤ ₱5M AND total assets ≤ ₱100M (excluding the land where the business sits); both conditions must hold. CREATE MORE (RA 12066, effective Nov 28, 2024) also gives 20% to registered business enterprises under the enhanced-deduction regime, but only on income from registered projects/activities; non-registered income stays at the regular rate, and EDR RBEs remain subject to the MCIT comparison.

value.startsInTaxableYear: 4th taxable year immediately following the year of registration with the BIR

legalBasis: RR 9-98 (the year operations commence is the year of registration with the BIR)
RR 12-2007 (quarterly MCIT on cumulative gross income)
RMC 36-2024 (computation for taxable years straddling Jul 1, 2023)
mcit.notes: Pay the higher of RCIT and MCIT (2% of gross income) from the fourth taxable year after the year the corporation registered with the BIR (RR 9-98), not the year of its first sale. When the profile has no registration year, the estimator shows both RCIT and MCIT with a warning. Excess MCIT over RCIT credits against RCIT for the next three years. The corporate estimator covers the current and the previous taxable year only (the default is the year whose annual return is due next, by the Manila date and the fiscal year); periods that start before Jul 1, 2023 are not supported, because MCIT and percentage tax were 1% from Jul 2020 to Jun 2023.

fiscalYear.value: Corporations may adopt a fiscal year; individuals must use the calendar year
legalBasis: NIRC Sec 47 (change of period needs prior CIR approval)
fiscalYear.notes: Quarterly returns fall 60 days after each of the first three quarters of the taxable year (no fourth quarterly return); the annual return falls on the 15th day of the 4th month after fiscal year-end.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 34(L), as amended by RA 9504
osdCorporate.notes: Corporations compute OSD on gross income (after cost of sales), unlike individuals who use gross sales/receipts. The election is signified on the first-quarter return and is irrevocable for the year, and unlike individuals, a corporation on OSD still submits financial statements with the annual return. The corporate estimator offers it as the 'Deductions' choice (OSD line rounded to whole pesos).

value.creditedAgainst: regular corporate income tax only, in a year when the regular tax is the tax due

excessMcitCredit.notes: Excess of MCIT over the regular tax is carried forward and credited against the regular tax of the next 3 taxable years, never against the MCIT. The estimator credits unexpired amounts oldest first, only when the regular tax is the tax due, up to the full regular tax, on the annual and the quarterly view. Whether the credit may bring the amount payable below that year's MCIT is not confirmed; check with a CPA.

improperlyAccumulatedEarningsTax.notes: No IAET is due for any taxable year ending after April 11, 2021. The SEC-side restraint survives: RCC Sec 42 still limits retained surplus beyond 100% of paid-in capital.
